principles.rule: Every approved K00 command maps to exactly one logical application command entry point owned by the command owning module.
HTTP, UI, jobs, CLI, agents, and automation invoke application command entry points; none owns business-rule semantics.
Caller-supplied identity, tenant, location, capability, or scope data is never authoritative; authoritative current facts are resolved server-side.
Authorization/target checks complete before any command side effect.
Cross-domain mutation invokes the owning module application command boundary; foreign repositories and foreign-table writes are forbidden.
Cross-domain reads use owner-defined read/query interfaces with explicit authoritative scope.
Required audit append participates in the same transaction as the mutation; audit failure rolls back the mutation.
Application orchestration may coordinate multiple owning modules in one transaction context without transferring write ownership.
External effects are invoked through infrastructure/provider ports; ambiguous outcomes enter TransactionControl reconciliation before retry.
Observability receives side-effect-neutral operation/request facts and cannot change authorization or command outcome.
Application results are transport-neutral; HTTP status/error-envelope mapping remains a Transport Interfaces decision.
Application Interfaces define logical use-case/read/port boundaries only; persistence tables, HTTP routes, and physical package paths remain deferred.

policy_and_cross_cutting_interfaces.purpose: Evaluate database-current actor scope, capability, target scope, and non-disclosing denial before protected work.
Append immutable required audit facts in the same transaction as the mutation.
Record request/operation observability without affecting request, authorization, or mutation result.
Read canonical provider state during reconciliation; no retry is implied by the interface.
